notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), no hardware was attached and no hardware run is claimed. WHAT IT SERVES: the card's models[0], mujoco_panda/models/franka_panda.xml, as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [...]}}; the bridge checks each ctrl element against the model's actuator_ctrlrange (nine channels: seven torque motors, +-87 for arm joints 1-4 and +-12 for joints 5-7, plus two gripper position actuators, 0 to 0.04) before data.ctrl is written, then runs mj_step ticks times. cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed). No bound is copied into a Limit: the envelope is derived from the model at run time and there is no site-limits.example.json. WHY THIS SHAPE: the card is family-config with helper MujocoDriver and the upstream is a MuJoCo-based Franka Panda simulator whose models are MJCF scenes (README.md:12-18); the card has no confirmed entry_symbols. The model is read from the read-only clone in place and is never copied into the package or imported. Only models[0] is served; the no-gripper, position-actuator and block-table scenes are other models and are not part of this driver. NOT COVERED: MuJoCo and mujoco_py were not importable where the gate ran (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is this package's stand-in mujoco module (fake.py). It parses the same MJCF file and its includes for the actuator control ranges, joint dimensions and option timestep, but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its control value; it treats the seven torque channels as position targets, loads no mesh or texture, resolves no contact, friction, tendon, equality or actuator constraint, and reads no force/torque sensor. The model sets no timestep, so the published timestep_ms comes from the stand-in's placeholder library default. No trajectory was compared with the real engine or the upstream mujoco_py simulator, no viewer or rendering is exposed, and no physical Franka Panda is modelled; the fidelity gaps list these differences. The real sim path (the official mujoco module loading the same scene) was not run. WARNINGS (none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco module rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder, and G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed inputs the simulator family derives; PLAYBOOK.md section 8 calls the latter expected for Gymnasium and MuJoCo drivers. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised. TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds six cases (model shape from the card scene, per-actuator control-range refusals with zero effect, state following the control value, reset to the model defaults, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass. No catalogue_requests: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used.
